label: Dismantled necessary causal connection between fire and burning
description: Al-Ghazali (Algazel) formulated and introduced the concept of "Incoherence of Necessary Causation", which became a seminal contribution in epistemology philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Formulating an epistemic apparatus to resolve central problems in epistemology.
historicalContext: Introduced during the Medieval & Islamic Golden Age as part of Al-Ghazali (Algazel)'s canonical writings.

label: Provoked Averroes' Tahafut al-Tahafut defending Aristotelian rationalism
description: Averroes (Ibn Rushd) wrote The Incoherence of the Incoherence to systematically vindicate pure Aristotelian philosophy against Al-Ghazali's theological assault, defending secondary causation and demonstrative proof.
dialecticalTension: Occasionalism and divine voluntarism versus Demonstrative rationalism and Aristotelian natural causality.
historicalContext: Cordoba and Marrakesh, c. 1180 CE. Averroes served as chief qadi and royal physician in Islamic Iberia.

citations.author: Averroes
citations.work: The Incoherence of the Incoherence (Tahafut al-Tahafut)
citations.quote: To deny the existence of efficient causes which are observed in sensible things is sophistry... Reason is nothing but the apprehension of causes.

label: Occasionalist causal critique anticipated Hume's Problem of Induction by 600 years
description: David Hume was fundamentally influenced by Al-Ghazali (Algazel)'s central inquiries, which shaped the evolution of their philosophical worldview.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Al-Ghazali (Algazel)'s perspective to David Hume's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the Medieval & Islamic Golden Age across history into the Enlightenment & Social Contract.
